summary:
I read every changed and added file and ran the slice's checks myself. The code matches the design. Every departure is either declared or was decided at critique (M1 to M5, m1 to m3). Nothing is wrong in the shipped code. The only items filed are one routing gap and one fragile default.

Measured in this review (pwsh 7.6.6, unelevated):

**The acceptance test**
- SL-098-RuleCasesUnlistableTemp.Tests.ps1 exits 0 with 4 of 4 checks ok, under the user's TEMP and under TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP.
- A mutant that puts Remove-Item back as the whole body of Remove-ScratchDir makes it exit 1. The output says 'C-006 stopped: Access is denied.', the Remove-Item error is raised inside the finally, and fsa-rulecases-<hex> and fsa-rules-* are left in the unlistable TEMP. The file was restored and git shows no change to it.

**RuleCases -Case All with the engine's real python** (through SL-098-RuleCasesUnderTemps.Tests.ps1)
- Under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP: exit 0, 'All checks held.', and no line says 'Access is denied', 'stopped:', 'cleanup:' or FAIL. The scratch line reported TEMP C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\ and a root in LocalAppData\Temp, and that root was gone afterwards.
- Under the ordinary TEMP: the same result.

**The other tests**
- SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1: all checks hold, including the repeat under powershell.exe 5.1. I read it as well, and each shape really is fed:
  - a read-only file under a Deny-ListDirectory parent, with a plain recursive delete shown to refuse it first;
  - a junction whose target holds a read-only file, with the walk also fed the junction directly;
  - a folder that is already gone;
  - a file held open with FileShare.None, which gives exactly one 'cleanup:' count.
- SL-098-ReturnValues.Tests.ps1: all checks hold, including the 5.1 repeat.
- SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1 passes under both TEMPs.
- SettledCountProbe -Shape BothShells passes under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP.
- The targeted Core tests under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP (CloudRigTests, TempTreeRootTests, LastAccessRuleCorpusTests, ArchitectureRulesTests, OptInTraitTests): 160 of 160 passed, including the new PrepareParent Fact.
- Fitness op=check: all 88 rules hold.
- Every changed .ps1 is ASCII. All are CRLF except the acceptance test, which is LF, as the repro wrote it.

**Not run by me**
- WindowMutants -Mutant All, which takes about 7 minutes on the desktop.
- SL-098-B008Root.Tests.ps1. I checked the pad arithmetic by reading: the root is exactly 250 characters for case folders of 65 and 83 characters.
- The opt-in Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT rig. Q-086 gives that run to validate, not to code review.

**Leftovers in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp**
Two folders, fsa-rulecases-0879ca0938 and fsa-rulecases-3bd86f4f0e, were created at 06:13:44 and 06:15:43 today. Each holds 134 fsa-parity-case-* and 6 fsa-engine-case-* folders. They were made after the build commit (06:13:22) and before the slice index was rewritten (06:21:08), so they come from the engine's own post-build proving runs, not from the fixed code. Every run I made removed its root. I did not delete them. Validate should not count them against this slice.

**Loop check**
There has been one build attempt, so the slice is not looping.

Second round: Second round: I tried to break the changed code and found nothing new. The two minor findings from round 1 still stand and are not repeated here.

**Remove-ScratchDir, run on shapes the first round did not cover** (extracted from RuleCases.ps1, run under pwsh 7.6.6 and powershell.exe 5.1)

| Shape | pwsh 7 | powershell.exe 5.1 |
|---|---|---|
| Read-only subfolder | removed, nothing counted | removed, nothing counted |
| Read-only top folder | removed, nothing counted | removed, nothing counted |
| Hidden+System+ReadOnly file | removed, nothing counted | removed, nothing counted |
| Nested read-only folders holding a read-only file | removed, nothing counted | removed, nothing counted |
| Path given with a trailing separator | removed, nothing counted | removed, nothing counted |
| A file at the path | left in place, nothing counted | left in place, nothing counted |

The file case is a no-op by design, and no caller passes a file.

**RuleCases.ps1 run whole under powershell.exe 5.1 with TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP**
- I ran -Case C-003 and -Case C-004. These cases make scratch, unlike the C-001-only SettledCountProbe run.
- Both exit 0 with 'All checks held.'.
- The scratch line shows a root in LocalAppData\Temp and TEMP C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\.
- Both roots were removed. This is the end-to-end 5.1 path that M3 was worried about.

**The new fitness rule, put through the engine's own comment stripping and its YAML pattern** (taad3.fitness.strip_comments)
- It fires on both old spellings, :182 and :859.
- It stays quiet on a '#' comment line.
- It misses a Remove-Item that follows a '#' inside a string on the same line. The engine blanks .ps1 text from any '#' to the end of the line without regard to strings, so no pattern can see it. That is an engine limit, nothing this diff caused, and not worth filing.

**Possible break checked and dismissed**
SL-069-EveryCaseFollowsCounts' SettledMarkers shape expects the last settled marker in .taad/fitness.yaml to be SL-069's. This slice appends '# settled by SL-098', but the last marker at HEAD 88e0824 was already SL-096. That expectation was already failing before this slice, so SL-098 caused nothing new there.

**Other boundaries read**
- Get-ScratchParent: a \\?\ spelling and a drive-root Windows folder, neither of which comes up on any measured setup.
- PrepareParent: a parent that exists as a file, which passes the IOException through.
- B-008 pad: the longest pad is 199 characters, under the 255 a single path segment allows, and the name never ends in a dot or space.
- The wrapper scripts' regexes: paths containing parentheses still parse correctly.
- Remove-ScratchDir output inside functions whose return value is used: nothing leaks.

All probe files and folders were removed, and the working tree is unchanged.

findings.claim: Part (a) of the accepted M5 decision is not carried by anything any more. M5 said validate runs `eng/dotnet.ps1 test ... --filter Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT` three times in a row, under the permission a person gave in Q-086. The build reported O-020 done, the engine closed it, and the build's follow-up sends the run to a PERSON to do once. That contradicts both Q-086 and M5. The obligations still owed are only O-001, O-014 and O-015, so validate has no open obligation to run the opt-in rig. The new SyncRootRig constructor path (PrepareParent, then the root under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests, then registration) can therefore merge without the rig ever running under the engine's TEMP. Derived 7 and SC-171's 'pass under the engine's TEMP' would rest only on the default-suite PrepareParent Fact. The rig's own remarks say validate runs the filter three times wherever that is allowed.
findings.evidence: In tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/CloudPlaceholderTests.cs:27-31, the class remarks say validate runs the filter three times where it is allowed. The M5 decision is accepted-pending, with part (a) 'validate runs ... three times in a row'. O-020 is DISCHARGED with the note 'The three-run Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT validate case from Q-086 is owed to validate'. The STILL OWED list holds O-001, O-014 and O-015 only. The build's follow-up begins 'PERSON: run the opt-in rig once under the engine's TEMP'.

quote.text: Where it is allowed, validate runs the filter

findings.fix: No code change. Record an obligation owed to validate-slice, in M5's own wording: under TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, run `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT` three times in a row. Afterwards check that no sync root is registered, that no CfProvider is running, and that %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests holds no fsa-cf-* folder. Per #201, record any failure not caused by the parent choice instead of blaming it on the routing. If the owner limits Q-086 to SL-049, the obligation goes to the person instead.

findings.claim: The wrapper's default -EngineRoot assumes the repository sits two levels below C:\Users\sshub\projets, which holds only for a slice worktree (projets\filesystem-analyser-v2-wt\SL-0xx). From the main checkout (C:\Users\sshub\projets\filesystem-analyser-v2, per `git worktree list`), '..\..\taad_v3\backend' resolves to C:\Users\sshub\taad_v3\backend, which does not exist. So after the merge, the documented commands at the head of the file (`... -Temp Engine` and `-Temp Ordinary` with no -EngineRoot) fail from the main checkout with 'the harness cases need the engine'. The header's claim, 'default the taad_v3\backend checkout beside the projects folder', is false there. It fails loudly and names the path, so it is not a false pass.
findings.evidence: tests/bugs/SL-098-RuleCasesUnderTemps.Tests.ps1:53. `git worktree list` shows the main checkout at C:/Users/sshub/projets/filesystem-analyser-v2 and the slice at C:/Users/sshub/projets/filesystem-analyser-v2-wt/SL-098.
findings.fix: Try '..\taad_v3\backend' and then '..\..\taad_v3\backend', taking the first that exists. Or require -EngineRoot as RuleCases.ps1 does, and put it in the header's command lines.

obligations.evidence: I ran `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/bugs/SL-098-RuleCasesUnlistableTemp.Tests.ps1`: exit 0 with 4 checks ok under the user's TEMP, and again under TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. With Remove-Item put back as the body of Remove-ScratchDir in tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1, it exits 1 with all four FAILs. The file was restored.

In tests/bugs/SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1 the junction shape removes the tree and leaves the target's ordinary file present and its read-only file still read-only. The walk on its own (the nested Open-Tree, extracted from RuleCases.ps1) unlinks the junction without following it. I ran it under pwsh and it repeats under powershell.exe 5.1: all ok. In RuleCases.ps1, Remove-ScratchDir/Open-Tree deletes reparse entries with a non-recursive Directory.Delete or File.Delete and never recurses into them.

I ran RuleCases -Case All with the real engine python through SL-098-RuleCasesUnderTemps.Tests.ps1 under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and under the ordinary TEMP. Both exit 0 with 'All checks held.'. Every New-TempDir folder now sits inside <parent>\fsa-rulecases-<10 hex>, one level below GetTempPath(), and no case depended on the old location.
The same acceptance run and mutant described under O-001.

I ran SL-098-RuleCasesUnderTemps.Tests.ps1 -Temp Engine: -Case All exits 0. It saw TEMP C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\, the root was in LocalAppData\Temp, and the root was gone afterwards. No line says Access is denied, stopped: or cleanup:.
I ran SL-098-RuleCasesUnderTemps.Tests.ps1 -Temp Ordinary: exit 0 with all checks held, and the TEMP it saw is the one asked for.

In SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1 the control shows a plain Directory.Delete refusing the read-only tree under the Deny-ListDirectory parent, and Remove-ScratchDir then removes it with nothing counted. I ran it.
The SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1 junction checks: the tree is removed, and the target keeps both files with the read-only attribute still set. I ran it.
SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1: a missing folder, and a folder removed twice, throw nothing and count nothing. In RuleCases.ps1 the Exists guard is the first statement of Remove-ScratchDir.
SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1: a file held with FileShare.None gives exactly one count, starting 'cleanup: <held>: ', and no throw. The same call removes the tree once the handle is released. I ran it.

tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:2212-2214 sets $pad = 250 - case length - 1, so the root is exactly 250 characters for a 65-character case folder. Spike 2 measured 428 at a 250-character root. SL-098-B008Root.Tests.ps1 feeds TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and asserts root 250 and a length over 400. I did not run the window case.
The same pad gives exactly 250 for an 83-character case folder. B008Root -Temp Both compares the lengths across TEMPs. Read, not run by me.
I did not run WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant All (about 7 minutes on the desktop). The WindowCases.ps1 diff is confined to Test-B008's root line.

tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/CloudRig.cs PrepareParent does CreateDirectory and then Sweep. CloudRigTests.TheRigsParentIsMadeBeforeItIsSweptAndSitsWhereTheTreesDo feeds a parent not yet made, a dead-pid root and a live-pid root. I ran the filtered Core tests under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP: 160 of 160 passed.
Retired by decided finding M1. SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1 Test-ScratchParent runs 10 path-rule rows and 4 refusal rows plus a live-process row, all ok under pwsh and under 5.1.

In .taad/fitness.yaml the only SL-098 entry is 'RuleCases removes nothing with Remove-Item', and there is no WindowCases rule. No Get-CloudRigParent exists in WindowCases.ps1, and its diff touches only Test-B008.
tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1 extracts Invoke-HarnessRaw, Remove-ScratchDir and Get-ScratchParent. I ran it under the user's TEMP and under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP: all checks held both times.

In RuleCases.ps1, Get-ScratchParent uses a regex in place of IsPathFullyQualified, and Remove-ScratchDir uses Attributes and GetFileSystemInfos (no LinkTarget, no EnumerationOptions). The TempRoots and ReturnValues 5.1 repeats pass, and SettledCountProbe -Shape BothShells passes under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP (I ran all three).

SL-098-RuleCasesUnderTemps.Tests.ps1 sets $env:TEMP and $env:TMP in its own process, runs the child with -File, and asserts the '(TEMP ...)' in the scratch line RuleCases.ps1:107 prints. I saw it report C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\ and the ordinary TEMP respectively.

The code half is done: CloudRig.PrepareParent with its default-suite Fact, which I ran under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, and the SyncRootRig constructor calls it. M5's part (a), the three validate runs of Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT, is not carried by any open obligation. See finding m1.
RuleCases.ps1 Remove-ScratchDir/Open-Tree recurses by hand, unlinks reparse points without following them, and skips no attributes. TempRoots feeds the walk a junction directly.

In RuleCases.ps1 the scratch line uses Write-Host, and Remove-ScratchDir and the early-return Check go through Out-Host inside Invoke-HarnessRaw. I ran SL-098-ReturnValues.Tests.ps1 (census, 27 plants, D01-D09, 5.1 repeat): all checks held.
The `because` of the RuleCases rule in .taad/fitness.yaml now says Fitness blanks .ps1 comments unless including_comments is true, and that the anchor is defence in depth.

cases.evidence: tests/bugs/SL-098-RuleCasesUnlistableTemp.Tests.ps1 puts a Deny-ListDirectory ACE on a folder under the user's temp, sets TEMP and TMP to it, and runs the real RuleCases -Case C-006 with a stand-in python that makes fsa-rules-* in %TEMP% and exits 2. RuleCases' own root lands in that same unlistable folder (its 'scratch:' line shows no-list\fsa-rulecases-*). The Remove-Item mutant turns all four checks red.

SL-098-RuleCasesUnderTemps.Tests.ps1 -Temp Engine sets TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and runs -Case All with the engine python, which covers C-002..C-009, C-012 and C-014. It asserts the TEMP the child saw. I ran it: exit 0.
The same wrapper with -Temp Ordinary sets TEMP=TMP=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp and asserts the child saw it. I ran it: exit 0.
SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1 builds 'control' with a +R file inside the Deny-ListDirectory folder, shows a plain recursive delete refusing it, then runs Remove-ScratchDir.

In TempRoots, the 'with-junction' tree carries a +R file, so the first Delete fails, plus a junction to an outside folder holding a +R file and an ordinary one. The 'walk' rows feed Open-Tree a junction directly, because Delete's first pass unlinks it before the walk would see it.
TempRoots: Remove-ScratchDir on 'never-made', and twice on 'twice', asserting no throw and no count.
TempRoots: a [System.IO.File]::Open with FileShare.None on leaf.txt is held during the call. It asserts exactly one 'cleanup: <held>: ' count, no throw, and then removal after Dispose.

SL-098-B008Root.Tests.ps1 sets TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP for the child WindowCases -Case B-008, which makes its case folder in GetTempPath()\fsa-window-cases (65 characters). It asserts 'a root of 250 characters' and a length over 400. Read only: I did not run it, since it needs the desktop.
The same test with %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp (an 83-character case folder). -Temp Both asserts equal lengths across the two TEMPs. Read only.
WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant All runs against the current, changed WindowCases.ps1. The fsa-cf listings part of the shape was dropped by M1. Not run by me.

CloudRigTests.TheRigsParentIsMadeBeforeItIsSweptAndSitsWhereTheTreesDo calls PrepareParent on TempTree.DefaultTestsRoot and asserts it lies outside the Windows folder. Under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP (where I ran it, 160 of 160 passing) that is the redirected LocalAppData\Temp\fsa-tests. It feeds the shape only when the suite runs under that TEMP, as the design's check command says.

Retired by decided finding M1: neither WindowCases listing looks for SyncRootRig's roots, so Get-CloudRigParent was never built. The slot went to the Get-ScratchParent rows in SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1. This is a decided removal, not a coverage gap.

Not material by design, and the reason still holds: being killed is not a branch in RuleCases.ps1, and the root's location is pinned by the -Case All runs I made. The two unremoved fsa-rulecases-* roots from 06:13 and 06:15 show leftovers are now findable in LocalAppData\Temp.
Not material by design, and the reason still holds: WindowCases.ps1:2213 is a one-line guard that refuses by name when $pad -lt 1, and reaching it needs a TEMP of about 200 characters.

drift: M5's because-text puts choose, create and sweep 'into one helper in SyncRootRig'. The build put it in CloudRig.PrepareParent, as M5's fix text named it. That is the only place a default-suite Fact can reach it, because SyncRootRig is private to the Trait-gated class. The build summary states it but does not mark it as a choice between the two wordings.

Standing rule on outside defects: the PowerShell Remove-Item workaround (IsReparsePointLikeSymlink lists the parent, PowerShell#16804) is unconditional and has no KnownWorkarounds entry. That matches the design's explicit key decision and is recorded as a deviation. It lives only in test scripts, a comment in RuleCases.ps1 names the defect and the upstream issue, and a setting would govern nothing the app does.

Get-ScratchParent returns the temp path with its trailing separator and reads LocalApplicationData through GetFolderPath, not $env:LOCALAPPDATA. Both are declared. Its at-or-under test (GetFullPath plus StartsWith) is not TempTree's Scanner.IsAtOrUnder over LongPath.NormalizeRoot, so the two can disagree for a TEMP spelled with a \\?\ prefix. No measured TEMP is spelled that way.

No undeclared departure was found. The SL-076 and SettledCountProbe rework, the m2 extras (the early-return Check and `& $change | Out-Null`) and the SystemRootTempRouteCorpus.json note edits are all declared.
